cause: Virtualization recycled offscreen ancestors and supplied no sticky projection.
implementation: Cache display ancestry and subtree ranges during model rebuilding; move original rows into a bounded sticky layer; reuse selection, commands, drag and lifecycle. Account for occlusion during keyboard/reveal and keep collapsed ancestors visible.

upstream.adopted: Enabled, seven rows maximum, 40 percent viewport; existing project 26px geometry retained.

ui.measurement_limit: Single Chromium input sample including polling; not a performance benchmark or physical wheel measurement.
ui.scope: Nested ancestor rows, direct mouse/keyboard collapse, sibling replacement, depth cap seven, short viewport 40 percent cap, bounded rows, no scroll reads, row identity, refresh/root cleanup, four light/dark zoom combinations, shared picker and Explorer history regression.

native.scope: Original Typora private desktop, production assets, 1000 nested files, bounded DOM, visible collapsed parent and unchanged editor content.

install_uninstall.scope: Final candidate install/check/restore-uninstall/reinstall/check/detach-uninstall/reinstall/check, startup modes 0/1/2/3, failure/cancel/rollback and user data retention.

local.shell_integration: Existing Directory menu ownership conflict preserved; workbench transaction and standard check passed

validation_notes: Initial native gate rejected installed Typora 1.14.15; failure retained in sticky_native_20261025.log. Checked frame.js theme, file and editor ports and pinned the exact ASAR only for the Explorer fixture. Final native run passed.
Final UI/native/installation runs followed the final row-order adjustment. Initial and final run evidence retained.
Initial npm build was invoked from repository root and failed before building; all successful candidate builds used enhancements/.
limits: No full UI suite, full native light/zoom matrix, physical user desktop gestures or other-platform acceptance.
Compact folders were already inactive and remain inactive; no compact-mode acceptance claim.
User running windows require normal restart; installation does not hot-replace them.
